content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day horizon; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the first 5–7 days.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 60+ in history) — cap forecast at 5–10% above peak observed in prior 7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to recent volatility; dampen forecast by 1–3% for days following high volatility (std dev > 2x rolling mean).
- Lagged response: model lags true price movements by 2–4 days; shift forecast forward by 1–2 days for short-term (1–7 day) horizon.
- High variance in late forecast days (days 25–30) — reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to match observed smoothing in true outcomes.
